provenance_note: The requirement families are adapted from public ERPNext product documentation. Dataset names, prices, thresholds, dates and seller answers are synthetic business configurations; they are not customer records, customer statements or field feedback.
selection_note: Ten distinct rule families are supported by four source documents. Tax-inclusive pricing and fixed discounts on Net Total are separate families. Currency precision and quotation expiry are not evaluated. Source count is not independent customer count.

sources.title: Pricing Rule | ERPNext Documentation
sources.documented_rule: Rules support quantity bounds, selected customers, overlapping-rule priority, combined-item thresholds, replacement rates and active dates. Multiple discounts may add percentages or compound, depending on configuration. Recalculate after changing eligibility; an ineligible rule must stop affecting the price.
sources.evidence_excerpt: With Apply Discount on Discounted Rate, ERPNext compounds successive discounts instead of adding their percentages.
evidence_sections: Important fields and what they mean
Set quantity, value, and validity conditions
important_limitations: The documentation does not specify numeric priority direction; the benchmark instead declares an explicit named precedence order.
Date boundaries, rates, thresholds and stacking choices are authored seller configuration, not asserted ERPNext defaults.

sources.title: Apply Discounts to Sales Transactions | ERPNext Documentation
sources.documented_rule: Additional discounts can use Net Total or Grand Total as their basis and can be fixed amounts or percentages. Net Total discounts change eligible item values; Grand Total discounts reference the post-tax total and recalculate relevant net and tax amounts. Displayed breakdowns depend on the tax template and rounding configuration.
sources.evidence_excerpt: The system recalculates the relevant item and tax amounts so the document remains internally consistent.
evidence_sections: Apply an additional discount to the transaction
important_limitations: Do not treat a Grand Total discount as keeping original tax unchanged. The source does not define one universal formula for every tax template.
The benchmark chooses a fixed discount on Net Total with a simple tax recalculation. Its tax rate, amount and rounding are synthetic configuration, not statutory guidance.

sources.title: Set Up Buy One Get One Free Offers | ERPNext Documentation
sources.documented_rule: A qualifying purchase can add a same-item or different-item promotional row at zero rate. Minimum purchase quantity and free quantity are configurable, including buy two get one.
sources.evidence_excerpt: Confirm that ERPNext adds the free row with a zero rate.
evidence_sections: Create a Buy 1 Get 1 Free rule
important_limitations: The article does not establish a universal repeated-bundle formula. The benchmark explicitly chooses floor(purchased quantity / 2) gifts as authored seller configuration, not an ERPNext default.
Stock reservation, delivery and accounting are outside this generated-demo benchmark.

sources.title: Tax Inclusive Accounting | ERPNext Documentation
sources.documented_rule: When an entered price contains one percentage tax, derive the net value by dividing the inclusive amount by one plus the fractional tax rate. Included tax is the difference; do not add that tax again. The documentation's 108-at-8-percent example produces net 100, tax 8 and total 108.
sources.evidence_excerpt: ERPNext back-calculates the tax and taxable value instead of adding the tax on top of the entered price.
evidence_sections: Apply the template to a transaction
important_limitations: The benchmark deliberately uses one inclusive percentage tax. Multiple dependent tax rows and jurisdiction-specific requirements are out of scope.
Tax rates, displayed precision and rounding policy are explicit synthetic configuration; a correct final total alone does not prove a correct tax breakdown.

global_limitations: Documentation provides business-rule provenance, not observed customer demand or salesperson satisfaction.
The ten families are one vendor's documented capabilities, not ten independent customers or ten production deployments.
Source support does not prove the generated application implements the rule; numerical and browser acceptance must verify that separately.
No source establishes that intent clarification improves generation. That is the paired experiment's hypothesis.
This registry stores short excerpts and paraphrases, not complete copyrighted pages.
